snippet.title: Genialer Blätterteig-Trick! 🎄 Weihnachtsdessert mit Toffifee in nur 10 Minuten
snippet.description:
Genialer Blätterteig-Trick! Entdecke dieses unwiderstehliche Weihnachtsdessert mit Toffifee, knackigen Nüssen und samtigem Karamell – das perfekte Rezept für die Festtage!

In diesem Video zeige ich dir Schritt für Schritt, wie du aus einfachen Zutaten ein spektakuläres Festtagsgebäck zauberst. Schnelle und süße Blätterteig Rezepte sind ideal für die kalte Jahreszeit: knusprig, aromatisch und im Handumdrehen fertig!

Praktische Tipps & Back-Tricks aus dem Video:
• Gleichmäßiges Aufgehen: Den Blätterteig-Boden in der Mitte vor dem Backen gründlich mit einer Gabel einstechen, damit der Rand herrlich blättrig hochgeht und die Mulde für die Toffifee-Füllung flach bleibt.
• Perfektes Haselnuss-Aroma: Die Haselnüsse vor dem Hacken in einer trockenen Pfanne rösten und die Schale mit den Händen abreiben – so entfaltet sich der volle Nussgeschmack.
• Cremiges Karamell ohne Klumpen: Für die Karamellsauce unbedingt heiße Sahne (33%) zum geschmolzenen Zucker und der Butter geben, damit sich alles seidig glatt verbindet.

Zutaten:
Für das Blätterteig-Gebäck:
-   Blätterteig
-   Haselnüsse
-   Toffifee
-   1 Ei + 20 ml Milch (zum Bestreichen)
-   Schokodrops
-   Mandelblättchen
    Backen: 30 Minuten bei 180 °C (360 °F)

Für das hausgemachte Karamell:
-   200 g Zucker
-   90 g Butter
-   130 ml heiße Sahne (33%)
-   Eine Prise Salz

Für den wärmenden Wintertee:
-   Himbeeren
-   Mandarinenschalen
-   Schwarzer Tee
-   1 Zimtstange
-   Honig
-   Heißes Wasser

snippet.title: Can a plane outrun the night? Near the poles, it can. #earth  #sunset #aviation #science #space
snippet.description:
The sunset sweeps round the Earth once a day, so it is fastest at the equator, 1,670 km/h (1,038 mph), and slower the closer you get to the poles. About two thirds of the way to the pole it moves at an airliner’s 900 km/h (559 mph), and nearer the pole a plane flying west overtakes it, so the Sun rises again in the west.

A what-if flight, simulated: no airliner can stay in the air that long.
Earth images: NASA. Engine sounds: real airliner recordings.
Music: Edvard Grieg, Morning Mood (Peer Gynt).

snippet.title: Why Do We Have 3 Or 4 Holes?
snippet.description:
The Atlas of Animal Holes poster is now officially on sale in our DFTBA shop: https://store.dftba.com/products/atlas-of-animal-holes-poster

In order to do the things an animal needs to do – eat, drink, breathe, make babies – stuff needs to come into our bodies, and other stuff needs to leave. That’s why we animals have holes. But exactly how many holes those jobs require – and which jobs each hole does – turns out to be wildly different from one animal to the next.


LEARN MORE
**************
To learn more about this topic, start your googling with these keywords: 
- Cloaca: the single all-purpose rear opening in many animals.
- Spiracle: A small opening in the body wall of insects and some arachnids, like scorpions, that lets air in and out of the respiratory system.
- Operculum: the bony flap that covers the gills on a fish’s head
- Urethra: The tube that carries urine from the bladder out of the body, and in males also carries sperm.
- Proglottid: One of the many body segments of a tapeworm, each with its own reproductive organs, which fill with fertilized eggs and break off to leave the host.

localized.title: Why Do We Have 3 Or 4 Holes?
localized.description:
The Atlas of Animal Holes poster is now officially on sale in our DFTBA shop: https://store.dftba.com/products/atlas-of-animal-holes-poster

In order to do the things an animal needs to do – eat, drink, breathe, make babies – stuff needs to come into our bodies, and other stuff needs to leave. That’s why we animals have holes. But exactly how many holes those jobs require – and which jobs each hole does – turns out to be wildly different from one animal to the next.


LEARN MORE
**************
To learn more about this topic, start your googling with these keywords: 
- Cloaca: the single all-purpose rear opening in many animals.
- Spiracle: A small opening in the body wall of insects and some arachnids, like scorpions, that lets air in and out of the respiratory system.
- Operculum: the bony flap that covers the gills on a fish’s head
- Urethra: The tube that carries urine from the bladder out of the body, and in males also carries sperm.
- Proglottid: One of the many body segments of a tapeworm, each with its own reproductive organs, which fill with fertilized eggs and break off to leave the host.

snippet.title: Why Factories Shoot Potatoes Through Knives
snippet.description:
Whole potatoes become fries by moving through blades that stay still. Water carries each potato through a narrowing tube that speeds it up and lines it up lengthways.

Fixed crossing blades divide it into strips. A widening outlet slows the pieces before a conveyor separates them from the water. Water supplies the push. The knives do the cutting.

snippet.title: Schwedens rote Häuser: mit Mehl gestrichen
snippet.description:
Falunrot, die rote Farbe der schwedischen Holzhäuser mit den weißen Ecken, wird aus Wasser, Roggenmehl, Leinöl und rotem Pigment im Kessel zu einem Brei gekocht. Das Pigment ist Abraum aus der Kupfergrube von Falun: eigentlich gelber Schutt, der erst beim Rösten im Ofen rot wird. Die Farbe blättert nicht ab, sie zerfällt zu Staub, und seit die Grube 1992 geschlossen wurde, kommt kein neuer Schutt mehr auf die Halden.

snippet.title: Rice Still Above ₹90/kg! But Telangana Farmers' Paddy Prices Have Fallen #riceprice #the4thestate
snippet.description:
Rice Still Above ₹90/kg! But Telangana Farmers' Paddy Prices Have Fallen
#Telangana #RicePrices #PaddyPrices #TelanganaFarmers #RiceMillers #FarmersIssues #Miryalaguda #Mahabubabad #AgricultureNews #RicePriceHike #PaddyMarket #the4thestate 

Rice prices in Telangana remain high despite the state government's warning to rice millers. But while consumers are still paying more than ₹90 per kg for premium rice, farmers are reportedly receiving much lower prices for their paddy.

On October 30, 2026, the Telangana government reportedly held a meeting with rice millers and warned them against increasing rice prices. Many expected prices to come down after the meeting. However, according to the figures discussed in this video, premium rice prices have continued above ₹90 per kg.

Meanwhile, paddy prices reportedly declined after the meeting.

Key figures highlighted in the video:

- Premium rice prices: More than ₹90 per kg.
- Ordinary rice prices: Approximately ₹66–₹67 per kg, according to the narration.
- Fine-quality paddy in Miryalaguda at the beginning of the season: Around ₹4,100 per quintal.
- Mahabubabad market price: Reportedly reached ₹4,580 per quintal.
- Paddy prices in several markets: Approached ₹5,000 per quintal.
- Current reported farmer prices: Around ₹3,300–₹3,500 per quintal.

The video raises an important question: If the government's meeting was intended to control rice prices, why have retail prices remained high while farmers' paddy prices have reportedly fallen?

Are farmers getting a fair price? Are consumers getting relief? And who benefits when the gap between paddy prices and retail rice prices remains so large?

Watch the full video and share your opinion in the comments.

Like, Share and Subscribe to The Fourth Estate for more Telangana agriculture, farmers' issues and economic updates.

Note: The market prices mentioned are figures cited in the video, not independently verified statewide averages. Paddy prices vary by variety, quality, procurement conditions and market. The timing of the price decline does not by itself establish that the millers' meeting caused it.
